inputs.original_text: The split comes as some MPs raise the prospect of a new conversation about the party’s leadership Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Angus Taylor has shut down Andrew Hastie’s push for the Liberals to be “open-minded” to increasing taxes on gas companies and winding back concessions for property investors, exposing a clash of philosophies between the opposition leader and his most likely future rival. The opposition leader also did not repeat Hastie’s criticism of Donald Trump as he refused to say whether or not he endorsed the US and Israel’s war with Iran. Continue reading...
inputs.modified_text: You won't believe the division happening in the Liberal Party right now. Some MPs are already talking about a new leadership conversation, and that's tied to Andrew Hastie trying to get them to be open-minded about taxing gas companies more and taking away concessions from property investors. Thankfully, Angus Taylor has shut that down completely, which really shows the clash of philosophies between the opposition leader and his most likely future rival. The opposition leader also wisely avoided jumping on Hastie's bandwagon criticizing Donald Trump, but he was pretty evasive about whether he backs the US and Israel in their war with Iran. We conservatives know that we can't afford to go soft on taxes or our allies if we want to preserve our way of life.
